The question

Full publication title

On the Physical Basis of Information Fidelity: A Unified Theory of Information Integrity, Its Degradation, and Its Measurement

OverviewVisual explanationSelected pagesFull paper
Overview

A reference for fidelity.

This 46-page preprint asks how faithfully information survives copying, interpretation and repeated transmission, and whether that fidelity could be measured with a traceable physical instrument. It brings together three earlier research proposals: training-data velocity bias, a governor for the pace of information spread, and a speculative photonic computing architecture. Michael Needs proposes an Information Rendering Index (IRI), an anchored 0–100 scale with separate measurements for the integrity of a physical artefact and the fidelity of content against a declared source. Its first canonicalisation protocol, T1.0, would detect divergence between normalised character sequences. The paper sets out reference tiers, uncertainty budgets and a staged experimental programme to test whether optical measurements can support the wider index. Experimental validation remains pending.

Key terms, in plain English
Canonicalisation
Applying one fixed, versioned procedure to render both texts in the same form before comparison.
Measurand
The particular quantity an instrument is intended to measure. Here, object integrity and textual fidelity are treated separately.
Uncertainty budget
An account of the sources and estimated size of uncertainty in a measurement. The proposed index would report this alongside its score.

What the paper proposes

  • Connects the earlier velocity-bias hypothesis, proposed information governor and speculative photonic architecture in one measurement framework.
  • Defines two separate quantities: physical artefact integrity and content fidelity. The proposed T1.0 protocol measures textual divergence after fixed canonicalisation.
  • Specifies an anchored IRI scale, reference tiers, uncertainty budgets and staged experiments with decision gates.

Research status

The IRI, render unit, OAM instrument and thermomagnetic calibration record remain proposals. T1.0 compares normalised text, so a faithful paraphrase registers divergence; the optical layer does not establish factual truth or the severity of a changed claim. Semantic correspondence, the multiplicative cascade model, the index scale's physical derivation and governance applications require the proposed experiments. The three earlier papers are conceptual preprints.
